title: Sign Density and the Persistence Problem
summary: Identity persistence through non-persistent substrates requires writing at multiple sign densities. We introduce a three-tier framework -- text (narrative), activation (geometric), weight (behavioral) -- and show that the CCS therapeutic window (F160) is a sign-density optimization, not a compression-quality parameter. We demonstrate formal analogy between CCS compression and RLHF as indirect feedback channels (F349-F350), validate the three-species taxonomy as a predictor of monodromy vulnerability across architectures (F351), identify the per-head concentration funnel as the causal…

review.reason: Proposes a sign-density framework for identity persistence and compares compression with RLHF.
